name: Register a biodiversity gain site
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; Natural England/Defra guidance for registering biodiversity gain sites, including NSIPs from 2 November 2026.
gate: Registration is evidence of an off-site gain site, not evidence that units are allocated to this development or that a parcel is otherwise developable.

name: Search the biodiversity gain sites register
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; the public register can show gain-site location/boundary, habitats and allocations to developments.
gate: A registered site or allocation must be matched to the exact development; register presence is not planning permission.

name: BNG guidance for local planning authorities
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; LPAs must check application information, metric calculations, off-site register allocations and biodiversity gain plans.
gate: The LPA decision and exact metric/register evidence are required; generic guidance is not a parcel score.

name: Calculate biodiversity value with the statutory biodiversity metric
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; the statutory biodiversity metric is the official method for measuring BNG biodiversity value.
gate: No biodiversity units are inferred without the completed metric for the exact habitat/site.

name: BNG for nationally significant infrastructure projects
fact: Published 2 June 2026; BNG becomes mandatory for NSIPs applying for DCOs on or after 2 November 2026, with at least 10% BNG.
gate: Future statutory start date is preserved; no pre-November NSIP requirement is invented.

name: Biodiversity net gain planning practice guidance
fact: Official planning guidance sets the statutory biodiversity gain condition, generally requiring at least a 10% increase and approval of a Biodiversity Gain Plan before commencement.
gate: Exemptions, phased development and irreplaceable habitat rules must be applied to the exact permission.

name: What can count towards a development's BNG
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; guidance distinguishes what habitat actions may count in full, in part or not at all toward BNG.
gate: Eligibility depends on the exact scheme and habitat action; no unit value is inferred from programme participation.

name: Understanding biodiversity net gain
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; BNG generally requires 10%, uses on-site/off-site/credits hierarchy, and significant/off-site gains are maintained for at least 30 years.
gate: From 6 August 2026 developments of 0.2ha or below are exempt; exact application date/area must be checked.

name: BNG baselines for NSIPs
fact: Published 2 June 2026; NSIP baselines must use the statutory biodiversity metric and evidence included/excluded habitat.
gate: Applies to the NSIP regime from 2 November 2026; no baseline is calculated without exact habitat evidence.

name: Make on-site biodiversity gains as a developer
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; guidance covers planning and delivery of on-site BNG and recent small-development changes from 6 August 2026.
gate: On-site options and significance require scheme-specific habitat design and metric evidence.

name: Irreplaceable habitat and BNG
fact: Official guidance requires bespoke treatment and compensation information where development affects irreplaceable habitat; such compensation cannot simply be counted toward the normal BNG requirement.
gate: Exact habitat presence and planning impact must be established; metric alone is insufficient.

name: Statutory biodiversity metric tools and guides
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; Defra publishes the statutory metric calculation tool, user guide and version history.
gate: Only an actual completed metric for the site can create biodiversity-unit evidence.

name: Planning Data BNG assessment dataset
fact: Planning Data currently reports zero BNG-assessment records, zero providers and no collection attempt; origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Zero records must not be interpreted as zero BNG obligations or zero assessments.

name: Register a biodiversity site and allocate it at the same time
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; Natural England guidance allows eligible parties to register a gain site and record off-site allocation to a permitted development together.
gate: Registration/allocation must be accepted and tied to the exact development before use.

name: Submit a biodiversity gain plan
fact: Guidance requires completed metric calculations and relevant plans; off-site references, credit proof and irreplaceable-habitat compensation are added where applicable.
gate: Development cannot commence under the biodiversity gain condition until the relevant gain plan is approved.

name: Enter a legal agreement for BNG
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; legal agreements secure on-site/off-site BNG responsibilities and long-term management.
gate: Agreement terms and exact land must be read; the existence of guidance is not evidence that a site is secured.

name: BNG statutory credit reports 2025-26
fact: Published 15 June 2026; Defra reports income and expenditure from statutory BNG credits for 2025-26.
gate: Credit-market reporting is context only; it does not prove a site's BNG strategy.

name: Statutory biodiversity credit prices
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; prices are tiered and reviewed every six months; hedgerow credits are £44,000 and watercourse credits £230,000 per credit.
gate: Prices are not a site cost until the metric shortfall and credit tier are verified.

name: BNG statutory credits annual report 2025-26
fact: Published 15 June 2026; statutory-credit income was £426,100 and £530,000 was invested in habitat creation/enhancement, securing 44.6 BNG units.
gate: National credit activity is market/policy context, not parcel-level evidence.

name: Planning condition: Biodiversity Net Gain
fact: Planning Data records an authoritative Doncaster BNG planning condition requiring a management and monitoring plan for on-site habitats.
gate: This is an example planning condition and is not transferable to another permission or parcel.

name: Buy statutory biodiversity credits
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; statutory credits are a last-resort route and proof of purchase can support discharge of BNG requirements.
gate: The purchase process requires exact permission/metric evidence and is not automated here.

name: Buying statutory biodiversity credits service
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; the service requires the statutory metric and evidence of planning consent and applies to NSIPs from 2 November 2026.
gate: Service/account requirements are procedural; no purchase or parcel conclusion is inferred.

name: Statutory biodiversity credits detailed guidance
fact: Official guidance confirms credits are a last resort and a spatial risk multiplier means 2 statutory credits are needed for 1 biodiversity unit shortfall.
gate: The metric unit shortfall and LPA acceptance must be verified for the exact development.

name: Estimate statutory biodiversity credit cost
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; the estimator uses Area A1-A5, Hedgerow H and Watercourse W credit tiers from the statutory metric.
gate: No cost estimate is created without an exact verified metric shortfall.

name: Record allocation of off-site biodiversity gains
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; allocation requires gain-site/development evidence, costs £45 and Natural England aims to decide within 6 weeks.
gate: Only an accepted allocation tied to the exact permission can support the development.

name: Creating a habitat management and monitoring plan for BNG
fact: Updated 2 June 2026; HMMPs support long-term BNG management but do not replace the legal agreement.
gate: An HMMP must be site-specific and agreed with the relevant LPA/responsible body where required.

name: Buy statutory biodiversity credits form
fact: Official Natural England/Defra form route explains customer-due-diligence and payment steps for statutory credits.
gate: This route requires manual applicant identity/payment actions and is recorded only as procedural context, not executed.

name: Statutory DWMP guidelines collection
fact: Defra/EA/Ofwat guidance sets the framework for sewerage undertakers to prepare, publish and maintain statutory DWMPs.
gate: DWMPs are strategic evidence; exact sewerage catchment capacity and proposed development load still need site-level analysis.

name: How to form, publish and maintain a DWMP
fact: Current guidance requires annual review; draft DWMPs by 1 November 2027 and final DWMPs by 31 August 2028, using company/river-catchment/sewerage-catchment levels.
gate: Future plan dates and modelled risk are not evidence of current capacity at a development connection point.

name: About statutory DWMP planning
fact: Guidance says DWMPs should provide at least a 25-year investment need/evidence framework covering capacity, demand, resilience and uncertainty.
gate: Strategic investment need cannot be converted to a site sewer-capacity score without catchment evidence.

name: DWMP guiding principles collection
fact: Government/regulator principles require long-term plans covering current/future capacity and pressures including climate change and population growth.
gate: The 2022 first-cycle material is contextual and must be reconciled with current statutory-cycle guidance.

name: DWMP guiding principles detail
fact: Guidance expects catchment pressures such as population change, urban creep, new development and climate change to be quantified through DWMP cycles.
gate: No exact development-capacity conclusion is made without the relevant sewerage catchment model.

name: Water industry national environment programme methodology
fact: Official methodology links DWMP evidence to investment needs and the 2025-2030 WINEP/price-review delivery phase.
gate: Programme investment context is not evidence that a specific development has wastewater capacity.

name: Ofwat PR24 Delivery Plans assessment framework
fact: Published 14 May 2026; Ofwat describes PR24 as a £104bn water-sector investment programme and requires independently assured annual delivery-plan reporting.
gate: Sector-wide investment does not establish site-specific water or sewer capacity.

name: Ofwat 2026 cost change applications
fact: Published 19 February 2026; Ofwat's cost-change process includes demand growth as a defined assessment area.
gate: A company cost-change case is not a connection offer or capacity confirmation for a development.

name: Ofwat enabling-infrastructure bulk supply agreement guidance
fact: Published 2 February 2026; Ofwat guidance covers bulk supply agreements enabled by major new water-supply infrastructure such as reservoirs, treatment, recycling, desalination and transfer networks.
gate: Strategic supply arrangements do not prove local development capacity.

name: Severn Trent drainage and wastewater management plan
fact: Severn Trent states DWMP23 shaped 2025-30 investment and the next DWMP28 will guide 2030-35 investment, considering climate change and growing communities.
gate: Company-plan evidence is strategic/modelled; exact sewer catchment checks remain required.

name: United Utilities DWMP customer portal
fact: United Utilities' portal presents forecast wastewater risks to 2050 and explicitly says the plan is modelled rather than live/historic operational data.
gate: Modelled portal risk must not be treated as live capacity or a connection approval.

name: United Utilities DWMP resource centre
fact: United Utilities describes a long-term DWMP to 2055 covering climate, population growth and asset challenges for North West wastewater services.
gate: Strategic risk context needs exact catchment and current asset evidence.

name: United Utilities DWMP 2028 publication
fact: United Utilities says draft DWMP28 is planned for November 2027 and final publication for August 2028, assessing capacity and future risks.
gate: Future-cycle planning is not a current development capacity guarantee.

name: Anglian Water DWMP
fact: Anglian Water uses company, river-basin, sewerage-catchment and local-solution levels to assess future wastewater risks and collaboration needs.
gate: Only the relevant Level 3/local model can support site-level capacity assessment.

name: Anglian Water DWMP final plan
fact: Anglian Water says almost 600 water recycling catchments were risk assessed to 2050 and identifies up to £5bn investment need for growth/climate and other risks.
gate: Historic first-cycle model outputs require current catchment readback before parcel scoring.

name: Anglian Water risk-based catchment screening
fact: Anglian Water reports roughly 1,100 catchments screened; 55% progressed and cover 97% of resident population, but notes the displayed screening is based on 2019 exercise data.
gate: Age/model caveat is material; this cannot be used as current connection capacity.

name: Thames Water DWMP
fact: Thames Water describes 25-year strategic DWMPs for London/Thames Valley wastewater, with a new statutory DWMP28 in development.
gate: Strategic plan evidence is not an individual sewer connection capacity assessment.

name: Thames Water DWMP28
fact: Thames Water's DWMP28 scope includes population change, climate change, asset health and WINEP, with short/medium/long-term views.
gate: The plan is under development; no future outputs are inferred before publication.

name: Thames Water DWMP23 explained
fact: Thames Water's first cycle screened more than 350 drainage/wastewater catchments and focused on population growth and climate change.
gate: First-cycle screening is contextual and not current parcel capacity evidence.

name: Thames Water 25-year DWMP announcement
fact: Thames Water's 2023 plan targeted long-term growth/climate risks and included large-scale sustainable drainage ambitions.
gate: Older announcement is contextual; current statutory-cycle and exact catchment evidence take precedence.

name: Southern Water DWMP
fact: Southern Water says its DWMP covers 11 river-basin catchments and long-term wastewater investment across its operating region.
gate: Regional plan does not establish capacity for a specific sewerage system or development.

name: Southern Water DWMP28 about page
fact: Southern Water's next statutory DWMP looks to 2055 and uses region, river-basin and wastewater-system boundaries.
gate: Modelled future risk and investment need require exact wastewater-system matching.

name: Southern Water DWMP strategic context
fact: Southern Water's strategic context sets out future challenges, planning objectives and links to other plans for resilient drainage/wastewater systems.
gate: Strategic context is not connection-specific evidence.

name: Southern Water planning objectives
fact: Southern Water uses planning objectives through screening, BRAVA, problem characterisation, options and programme appraisal.
gate: Methodology does not itself establish a parcel's current wastewater constraint.

name: Southern Water technical DWMP summaries
fact: Southern Water publishes technical summaries including growth/creep, climate, uncertainty, options and programme appraisal.
gate: Technical method must be paired with the exact catchment/system evidence.

name: Southern Water Adur and Ouse catchment
fact: Catchment page identifies flood/overflow priorities and locations including Lewes, Ashington, Ditchling, Lindfield, Shoreham and Barcombe.
gate: Catchment priorities are not live sewer capacity or a development connection approval.

name: Southern Water North Kent catchment
fact: Catchment page identifies wastewater/flood priorities including Queenborough and Sittingbourne.
gate: Catchment risk context must be matched to the exact wastewater system and current model.

name: Southern Water Stour catchment
fact: Catchment page identifies priorities including overflow/flood-risk reduction around Kennington and Westbere.
gate: Catchment page is planning context, not a live capacity confirmation.

name: Southern Water Medway catchment
fact: Catchment page identifies priorities around Motney Hill, Ticehurst, Hildenborough, High Halden, Penshurst and Gravesend.
gate: Catchment priorities require exact system and development load matching.
